dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: The type of admissible computation packages. By D003, such a package contains an addition model and a two-output real addition operation satisfying identification, exact-recovery, and residual-bound laws.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The universally quantified fp parameter supplies the operation used to compute every running sum and residual. Quantification is restricted to packages satisfying the bundled laws.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002
dependency_coverage.meaning: For an input v of length n+1, this defines an output of length n+1 whose indices below n contain the residuals from D004 and whose last index n contains the final accumulator from D005.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is the summand on the left-hand side. The conclusion states that the exact sum of this transformed output equals the exact sum of v.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef003
dependency_coverage.meaning: Constructor for D001. It takes a model M, an operation twoSum(a,b)=(q,r), and laws q=M.fl_add(a,b), q+r=a+b, and |r| <= M.u|q| for every a,b.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The exact law q+r=a+b is the per-step conservation identity underlying the conclusion. The identification with modeled addition and the residual bound restrict admissible fp values but are not asserted in the conclusion.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef004
dependency_coverage.meaning: For i in Fin n, it returns the second component of twoSum(S_i,v_{i+1}), where S_i is the prefix accumulator defined by D005.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: These are exactly the first n entries of the transformed vector and provide the correction terms that telescope with the running accumulator.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef005
dependency_coverage.meaning: For k <= n, it initializes an accumulator at v_0 and applies the first component of twoSum successively using the entries v_{i+1} indexed by i in Fin k. Under the standard Fin.foldl order, this gives S_0=v_0 and S_{j+1}=fst(twoSum(S_j,v_{j+1})).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It defines every prefix accumulator S_k, including the final transformed entry S_n and the input accumulator used to form each residual.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef006

binders: fp is an arbitrary admissible package of type LocalDef001, containing an addition model and a two-output operation twoSum on pairs of real numbers.
n is an arbitrary natural number, including n=0.
v is an arbitrary function Fin(n+1) -> Real, equivalently a real tuple (v_0,...,v_n) of exactly n+1 entries.
hypotheses: There are no separate implication hypotheses; all computational assumptions are bundled into the type of fp.
The model contained in fp has a real constant u with 0 <= u and an operation fl_add such that fl_add(0,x)=x for every real x.
For every real x,y, there exists a witness delta depending on x and y such that |delta| <= u and fl_add(x,y)=(x+y)(1+delta).
For every real a,b, writing twoSum(a,b)=(q,r), one has q=fl_add(a,b), the exact identity q+r=a+b, and the scalar bound |r| <= u|q|.
conclusions: If W is the transformed vector defined below, then its exact real sum is preserved: sum_{i=0}^{n} W_i = sum_{i=0}^{n} v_i. Equivalently, S_n + sum_{j=0}^{n-1} E_j = v_0+v_1+...+v_n, with the residual sum empty when n=0.
mathematical_definitions: Write twoSum(a,b)=(q(a,b),r(a,b)), where q is the computed first component and r is the residual second component.

For 0 <= k <= n, S_k is the D005 fold initialized at v_0 and updated over i in Fin k by s := q(s,v_{i+1}). Under the standard ascending Fin.foldl order, S_0=v_0 and S_{j+1}=q(S_j,v_{j+1}) for 0 <= j<n.
For 0 <= j<n, define E_j=r(S_j,v_{j+1}). The bundled exactness law gives S_{j+1}+E_j=S_j+v_{j+1}; also |E_j| <= u|S_{j+1}|.
Define W in Real^{n+1} by W_j=E_j for 0 <= j<n and W_n=S_n. This W is exactly LocalDef002 fp v.
The left-hand finite sum is therefore E_0+...+E_{n-1}+S_n, while the right-hand finite sum is v_0+...+v_n.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every admissible modeled addition package, every natural n, and every real vector of length n+1, start with v_0 and successively combine the current accumulator with v_1 through v_n using the first output of twoSum. Store the second output from each step as a residual, and finally store the last accumulator. The exact sum of the n residuals together with that final accumulator equals the exact sum of all n+1 original entries.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The input and output dimensions are exactly n+1, so they are always nonempty. The case n=0 is not vacuous: the fold performs no additions, W_0=S_0=v_0, and the conclusion reduces to v_0=v_0.

The computation is a sequential prefix fold beginning at v_0; under the standard Fin.foldl semantics, entries are processed in increasing order v_1,...,v_n. No claim is made for a different accumulation tree or permutation.

All values and equalities are in the exact real numbers. The proposition does not encode finite representability, overflow, underflow, exceptional values, or execution by a concrete hardware floating-point format.
The only magnitude operation is scalar absolute value. No vector norm, forward-error bound, backward-error bound, or stability estimate appears in the conclusion.
The theorem concludes only conservation of the total sum. It does not assert componentwise equality between W and v, nor does it bound the final accumulator or the sum of residuals.

The assumptions q=fl_add(a,b), the relative-error model for fl_add, fl_add(0,x)=x, 0 <= u, and |r| <= u|q| are stronger than needed for the displayed conservation equality; the per-step exact identity q+r=a+b is the law directly responsible for it.
No upper bound such as u<1 is imposed on the model parameter u.
The existential relative-error witness delta may depend separately on each ordered pair (x,y); no global delta or selected witness function is encoded.

The target universally quantifies over fp but does not itself assert that LocalDef001 is inhabited. Consequently, viewed in isolation, its fp quantification would be vacuous if no constructor arguments satisfying D003 existed.
ambiguities: The displayed body of Fin.foldl delegates to an omitted private loop. The conventional and intended reading is an ascending traversal of indices 0,...,k-1, which yields the stated recurrence for S_k, but that traversal order is not independently derivable from the private-loop body supplied in the dossier.
